learningObjectives: Describe flexible cognitive control as a network process.
Identify common lateral frontal and parietal components.
Explain adaptive coupling with other networks.
Relate control demand to fatigue and clinical performance.

anatomy.label: Lateral prefrontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Lateral prefrontal regions represent task rules, context and goal-relevant information.
anatomy.clinical: Performance may decline when working-memory and monitoring demands exceed capacity.

anatomy.label: Posterior parietal cortex
anatomy.detail: Parietal nodes support selection, evidence integration and flexible mapping between goals and responses.
anatomy.clinical: Relevant to set shifting, calculation, praxis and attentional control.

anatomy.label: Monitoring systems
anatomy.detail: Control systems compare performance with goals and recruit adjustment when needed.
anatomy.clinical: A person may be accurate yet exhausted if monitoring remains effortful.

anatomy.label: Adaptive coupling
anatomy.detail: Frontoparietal regions change their connectivity depending on whether a task requires memory, attention or internal simulation.
anatomy.clinical: Flexibility may matter more than globally high activation.

anatomy.label: Control cost
anatomy.short: Effort is metabolically and subjectively costly
anatomy.detail: Sustained control competes with fatigue, stress, reward and motivation.
anatomy.clinical: Executive performance should be assessed across time and complexity, not one easy task.

interaction.title: Frontoparietal Control Network sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow information flow across the network.

stages.label: Set goal
stages.text: Represent the rule, target or desired outcome.

stages.label: Configure
stages.text: Recruit the systems needed for the current task.

stages.label: Monitor
stages.text: Compare ongoing performance with the goal.

stages.label: Adjust
stages.text: Update strategy, effort or network coupling.

quizBank.question: The frontoparietal control network is especially relevant to:
quizBank.explanation: It supports flexible coordination under goal demand.

quizBank.question: A core principle of this network is:
options: Its coupling changes with task context
It works independently of all other networks
It is active only in childhood
More activation always means better performance
quizBank.explanation: Adaptive coupling is central to flexible control.

quizBank.question: Executive fatigue may occur when:
options: Accurate performance requires sustained high control effort
quizBank.explanation: Compensation can preserve accuracy at a high subjective cost.

quizBank.question: Lateral prefrontal regions often help maintain:
quizBank.explanation: They contribute to context and goal representation.

quizBank.question: Clinical executive assessment should consider:
quizBank.explanation: Executive performance is highly context sensitive.
